title: Gradient-factor MEND editor emitting a shared-basis Mirror code
hypothesis: A learned editor emitting a compact rank-2 code preserves held-out edit efficacy at lower actual bytes/compute than generic full-update MEND; Mirror-specific benefit must exceed native low-rank MEND.
storage: Actual serialized inference .npz payload including editor weights, shared basis, base layer, schema and key metadata.
success_gate: Both development seeds: Mirror nRMSE <=0.05, <=75% generic MEND payload bytes, and no latency/compute regression; Mirror-specific success additionally requires strict gain over native low-rank MEND.
failure_gate: Quality/storage/compute miss or native low-rank MEND exact alias. Fresh remains sealed.
boundaries: Fixed-budget learning-efficiency screen, not capacity claim
No pretrained model or real factual edits
